10.3: Raag Asa, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji): So Purakh. Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. That Purakh, the Being who pervades all, is Niranjan, free of the stain of Maya (the world's illusion and lure); the Lord, the all-pervading Being, is free of that stain; the Lord is beyond reach, wholly beyond reach, without limit. O Lord, the eternal Creator, all meditate on you, all meditate on you. All beings are yours, Lord; you are the Giver to every being. Meditate on the Lord, revered Sants (saints): he makes all sorrows pass away. The Lord himself is the Master, and the Lord himself the servant; O Nanak, what is a poor creature (by itself)? You are within every heart, and in all without any gap; O Lord, you, the one Being, pervade all. Some are givers and some are beggars; all these are your wondrous plays. You are the giver yourself, and yourself the one who enjoys (the gifts); apart from you I know no other. You are the Supreme Lord (Paarbrahm), endless, endless; which of your virtues shall I name and describe? Those who serve you, those who serve you, Lord: your servant Nanak is a sacrifice to them. O Lord, those who meditate on you, who meditate on you, live at peace in the world. Liberated, liberated are those who have meditated on the Lord; the noose of Jam has snapped for them. Those who have meditated on the Fearless, on the Fearless Lord: he takes away all their fear. Those who have served, who have served my Lord, merge into the very form of the Lord, Har Har. Blessed, blessed are those who have meditated on the Lord; your servant Nanak gives himself in sacrifice to them. The storehouses of devotion to you, of devotion to you, Lord, are full beyond end, beyond all end. Your devotees, your devotees praise you, O Lord, many, countless, without end. Many, so many, worship you, O Lord; numberless (beings) practise austerities and repeat (your Name). Many, so many of yours read the many Simritis and Shastras, and carry out the rites and the six duties. O servant Nanak, those devotees, those devotees alone are good who are pleasing to my Lord God. You are the Primal Being, beyond the farthest beyond, the Creator, Lord; no other is as great as you. In every age you are the One; always, always you are the One; you are the unmoving Creator, ever the same. O Lord, whatever pleases you yourself, that alone comes about; whatever you yourself do, that takes place. You yourself brought forth the whole creation, and you yourself, having made it, have destroyed it all. Servant Nanak sings the virtues of the Creator, who knows each and every one. ॥5॥
So Purakh, taken from the opening words of this shabad, is the heading of four shabads, which are read in Rehras, the evening bani.
Niranjan: nir (without) and anjan (collyrium, black stain); the One on whom the stain of Maya does not fall.
Ji, in nearly every line of this shabad, is a word of reverence for God.
ਜਨੁ ਨਾਨਕੁ (with the aunkar) is the subject: servant Nanak himself is the sacrifice; ਜਨ ਨਾਨਕ (without it) is an address, O servant Nanak, or, with a postposition understood, of servant Nanak.

The Simritis are the Hindu books of conduct and law, the Shastras the books of the six schools of philosophy; the six duties (khat karam) are a Brahmin's: to study and to teach, to perform sacrifice and to have it performed, to give alms and to receive them.
11.1: Raag Asa, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). You are the Creator, the abode of truth, my Master. Whatever pleases you, that alone will be; whatever you give, that alone I receive. All (creation) is yours; all have meditated on you. The one to whom you show grace has found the jewel of the Naam. The Gurmukh (one who follows the Guru) found it; the manmukh (the self-willed) lost it. You yourself have parted (beings from you), and you yourself have united (them). You are the river; all is within you alone. Apart from you there is no other. All beings and creatures are your play. By the will that parts, even one who had met is separated; by the will that unites, there is meeting (again). Only the one whom you make to understand comes to know (you), and he ever speaks and tells of the Lord's virtues. Whoever has served the Lord has found peace; in Sahaj (natural, unshaken poise) he has merged in the Name of the Lord. You yourself are the Creator; all that happens is your doing. Apart from you there is no other, no second. You create and create, watch over (your creation), and know all about it. O servant Nanak, (the Lord) is revealed within the Gurmukh. ॥4॥
Sachiar: sach and alaya (abode), the abode of truth, God who ever abides.
ਸਭ ਤੇਰੀ ਤੂੰ ਸਭਨੀ ਧਿਆਇਆ: here ਤੂੰ means you as the object (ਤੈਨੂੰ), and ਸਭਨੀ means by all.
Vijog and sanjog: the powers of God's will that part beings and bring them together.
12.1: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). (Our) dwelling has come to be in that terrible lake whose water he himself has made fire. In the mire of attachment the foot cannot move; before our eyes (many) have drowned there. O mind, O foolish mind, you do not remember the One. As you forget the Lord, your virtues have wasted away. I am neither celibate (jati) nor virtuous (sati), nor am I learned; my life has turned out the life of a foolish, ignorant one. Nanak humbly prays: (let me be) in the refuge of those who have not forgotten you. ॥2॥
The saravarra is a lake, here the world: its water is the fire of craving and its mire attachment. Pankaj here is not the lotus but the mire (pank).
Bhaile and dubiale are past forms of an eastern dialect: has come to be, have drowned.
12.2: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). You have received this lovely human body; this is your turn to meet Gobind (the Lord of the universe). All other tasks are of no use to you at all; join the Saadh Sangat (the company of the holy) and remember the Naam alone. Set yourself to the task of crossing the ocean of the world; your life is passing in vain in the love of Maya. (O Lord,) I have practised neither repetition (of the Name), austerity, self-restraint nor any deed of dharma; I have not served the Saadh (the holy one), nor have I known you, O Lord, my King. Says Nanak, we are of lowly deeds; save the honour of one who has come into your refuge. ॥2॥
The first six lines counsel the soul; in the last four Nanak prays humbly to God on behalf of all beings.
